narrative:
The model estimated a 43% chance that you would default on this loan, which is high enough that the bank decided to deny the application. This does not mean you will definitely default, but rather that your financial profile carries too much risk for approval.

What most influenced this decision? Interestingly, the amount you requested—3,804 DM, higher than the typical approved applicant’s 3,020 DM—was not the problem. In fact, it slightly worked in your favor, suggesting the model saw some offsetting strength in that larger request. The real concerns were your checking account and your credit history. Your account balance of 0 to 200 DM is a common pattern among risky applicants; only about 18% of approved applicants had such a low balance, compared to a majority who had no checking account or a healthier one. More importantly, your credit history shows no credits or all paid off. While that might sound positive, in this model it is actually a strong warning signal: only 1% of approved applicants had this type of record, whereas the vast majority had an established history of paid loans with the bank. This lack of proven repayment experience made the model more cautious.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a track record: consider opening and maintaining a checking account with a higher balance, and take on a smaller, manageable credit that you repay consistently. Adding a guarantor or reducing the loan amount could also help offset the perceived risk. These steps will show future lenders that you can handle credit responsibly.
